Main text in one column, full width; a catchword or note block is not present. The ornament and INDEX are printed at the foot and are transcribed as described below.

main_text.p: des lib.2.) ignominia tristior est morte, quæ cum gloria & spe publicæ salutis sine longo cruciatu aditur. Et ut Cicero docet Philipp.3. Mors servituti anteponenda est: quæ nihil est fœdius aut miserius: cum ad decus & libertatem nati simus: quam aut tenere, aut cum libertate mori debemus. Et Philipp.2. Pax est tranquilla libertas: servitus postremum malorum omnium, non modò bella sed morte etiam repellendum. Et quia populus Romanus nihil quidquam aut Samnitibus victoribus, aut etiam Numantinis promisit: sed Consules tantùm & Tribuni militum: (nec enim Consulis jus, nec sui erat arbitrii, pacem spondere:) ideo refcissâ turpissimâ pace, ejus auctores captivos hostibus dediderunt: atque ita pactis istis se liberarunt. Utique enim, quod belli cum est, duces belli tractare decet, non aliud: autipsi suo malo soli obligantur.
Plura de pacis observantiâ requirę lib.3. Stratagematographiæ nostræ cap.2.

page.notes: Woodcut ornament (winged cherub with a shield/cartouche) between the text and INDEX; not transcribed as text. The word INDEX at the foot is printed in large capitals and is set off from the text; it is a running label or section title on this page and is given here as a plain word. Some words in the text are italic as shown. Possible printing errors left as printed: "requirę" and "Stratagematographiæ" (the original line-break "Stratagema-/tographiæ"). Low confidence on the exact spelling of "requirę", "cap.2." and the exact wording after "populus Romanus"; the scan is faint in these places.
